newsitem.title: CANADA: Toronto stocks end lower on gold, U.S. weakness.
newsitem.headline: Toronto stocks end lower on gold, U.S. weakness.

text.p: Toronto stocks ended lower after a hectic session on Thursday, weighed down by weak golds and slipping Wall Street stocks.

The Toronto Stock Exchange 300 Composite Index fell 9.28 points to 5864.85 in heavy turnover of 109.6 million shares worth C$1.66 billion ($1.2 billion). Declining issues outnumbered advances 522 to 439, with 293 issues flat.
"The golds were weaker here, and I mean that's still a large part of our index, so that dragged us down," one trader said.
The gold sector shed more than 217 points or 2.42 percent, leading nine of Toronto's 14 sub-indexes lower. Metals and minerals were also hit, falling nearly 61 points or 1.16 percent to 5175.52.
Transportation, forest products, industrials, oils and merchandising ended the session in positive territory.
The trader said Canadian stocks were also dragged down by losses on Wall Street.
"The Dow wasn't that good. The breadth was never to the real positive side. It would have been down a lot more if it hadn't been for IBM," said one trader.
Shares of International Business Machine Corp. closed up 11-3/8 at 153-3/4 in New York after it released better than expected first-quarter results after Wednesday's close.
Bre-X Minerals Ltd. again topped Toronto actives, giving up early gains to end down 0.02 at 3.60 in turnover of more than 10.3 million shares.

Investors are trying to work through the details of developments surrounding the troubled Calgary, Alberta prospector's Busang gold field in Indonesia. The company's stock has been pounded in recent weeks by questions about the value of the deposit.
Strong quarterly earnings propelled a several stocks higher in Toronto.
Canadian National Railway Co. ended up 3.50 at 53.20 after reporting a first-quarter profit of C$1.51 a share on Thursday, versus year earlier C$0.92.

Fertilizer firm Potash Corp. of Saskatchewan Inc. closed at 105.95, up 1.35 on the day. Despite a fall in first-quarter earnings to $1.18 a share from $1.40 last year, the firm posted its second highest quarterly income ever of $56.4 million.
Moore Corp. Ltd. shares gained 0.80 to 29.10 in healthy trade after Moore reported higher earnings after Wednesday's close.
